objective: Help business owners understand when asset-specific finance suits better than a general business loan.

slides.headline: Asset Finance vs Business Loan
slides.subheadline: Financing tied to the asset, or general-purpose funds?

slides.headline: What's the real difference?
slides.body: Asset finance is structured specifically around a vehicle, machine or piece of equipment, often using the asset itself as security. A general business loan can fund almost any purpose and isn't tied to a specific item, which can mean different security and documentation requirements.

slides.headline: Asset finance may suit if
bullet_points: You're buying a specific vehicle or machine
You want the asset to secure the loan
You'd like the term matched to asset life
New or used equipment is being purchased
You want a straightforward, purpose-built structure

slides.headline: A business loan may suit if
bullet_points: You need funds for multiple uses
You don't want security tied to one asset
You're funding working capital as well
You want flexibility in how it's used

slides.headline: Purpose-built or general-purpose — match the tool to the job.
slides.body: If it's one specific asset, asset finance may be the simpler fit; broader needs may suit a general facility instead — subject to lender assessment.

caption:
Buying a specific vehicle or machine is a different funding problem to funding your business more broadly, and the two products reflect that.

Asset finance is purpose-built around one item, often using that asset as its own security. A general business loan is more flexible in purpose but isn't tied to — or secured by — any single item.
